title: Robert Bell — identity route

working_title.brake: The title is hotter than the present controlled body. The folio preserves it as a question-bearing flare, not as an independent historical finding.

body.job: Lay out the family testimony, early Bell and McKinney occurrences, the Commission's comparator, later review, and the surviving open questions without making unlike evidence interchangeable.
current: The federal record establishes an administrative refusal of MCR 879.
The Commission rejected the proposed identity between the family's Robert Bell and the previously adjudicated Article XIV Robert Bell.
Indian Affairs later stated the administrative conclusion as two Robert Bells.
The 1907 rehearing motion was denied on timeliness grounds.
does_not: The body does not convert the federal identity finding into an independent historical identity finding.
The body does not establish that the early Public Lands Robert, James, and Levy Bell are the family configuration later described in MCR 879.
The body does not establish that Catharine McKinney in Article XIX is the family's Catherine/Catharine McKinney.
The body does not establish what procedural or substantive position the Choctaw Nation took after notice to its attorneys.

route.label: Family knowledge enters
route.text: Mary Caroline Atkinson and William D. Bell describe Robert Bell through family memory, reported enrollment, purchased land, and uncertainty about Article XIV.

route.label: Identity machinery sharpens
route.text: Hugh, Thrace, and Emma encounter Article XIV questioning and the older federal Robert Bell comparator. Knowledge, examiner wording, and family correction remain separate.

route.label: Robert / James / Levy occur independently
route.text: Public Lands No. 3 contains Robert Bell, James Bell, and Levy Bell within the same surviving documentary body. The manuscript itself does not state that they are related or identify them as the later MCR 879 family.

route.label: Two bodies compared
route.text: The Commission compares the family's Robert Bell with the previously adjudicated Article XIV Robert Bell and treats the differences as sufficient to reject identity.

route.label: Administrative finding hardens
route.text: Indian Affairs identifies the Robert Bell identity question as decisive and recommends affirmance. Interior affirms.

route.label: Question changes
route.text: The rehearing motion is denied pro forma as untimely. The record is not transmitted because the Office says it is unnecessary for deciding that motion.

machine_lenses.question: What happens to the family's statements as the examiner supplies wording and later administration summarizes them?
machine_lenses.use: Keep heard / told / saw / does not know / examiner-supplied language separate. Hugh's 'I suppose so' does not become three assents merely because the question carried three propositions.
returns: Hugh recognition turns on one source face, separately addressable.

machine_lenses.question: What lower acts and carriers make the compact administrative answer 'two Robert Bells' possible?
machine_lenses.use: Open the finding downward into family testimony, comparator record, residence, wife, company, registration testimony, and patent material without treating the finding itself as an independent historical proof.
returns: Commission decision p.-45- and separately labeled lower dependencies.

machine_lenses.question: What changes when Robert / James / Levy are viewed as a configuration rather than isolated names?
machine_lenses.use: Show the later family relation and the earlier Public Lands name configuration side by side without joining identities automatically.
returns: Public Lands rows and family testimony remain separately governed.

machine_lenses.question: Which proposition is being carried, changed, supplied, refused, or left open at each step?
machine_lenses.use: Follow the identity proposition and the Article XIV compliance proposition separately so closure of one does not silently close the other.
returns: State-local passage, governing face, and larger object remain distinct.

return_rules: SAME SOURCE FACE ≠ SAME MACHINE STATE.
ONE REPRESENTATION MAY SERVE SEVERAL RETURNS; EACH RETURN MUST NAME ITS LOCAL TURN.

questions: What early record was the family describing when it spoke of Robert Bell being registered?
What record did Thrace Bell see the day before her examination?
What roll did Emma Pickens describe as being held by a lawyer?
What weight should be given to the independent early occurrence of Robert, James, and Levy Bell in Public Lands No. 3?
What relation, if any, exists between the Bell–McKinney family and Catharine McKinney in the separate Article XIX record?
What record population did the Commission actually search when it made its negative McKinney statement?
What procedural or substantive position, if any, did the Choctaw Nation take after notice was sent to its attorneys?
What later federal act, if any, reached beyond the administrative identification question decided in MCR 879 and closed a broader treaty claim?

conversation_reading.glint: 15 is learning how an object becomes traversable while the folio is learning how a person traverses an object.
conversation_reading.present_recommendation: Operate the machines on the body rather than merely describing them. Keep enough source language on screen that a person can see what changed, refuse false transitions, and carry a live question into Notes without reconstructing the record from memory.

hugh_recognition.title: Hugh G. Bell · recognition exchange · Atoka · 27 Mar 1901
hugh_recognition.source_object: MCR 1546 Hugh G. Bell sworn examination

turns.speaker: Commission
turns.text: Was he recognized by the Choctaw tribal authorities as a Choctaw Indian?

turns.speaker: Hugh G. Bell
turns.text: Yes, that is what they tell me; I have heard them say he was.
turns.reading: Hugh reports what others told him and what he heard. He does not claim personal knowledge of the recognition act.

turns.speaker: Commission
turns.text: Well, by the tribal authorities, I mean by act of council did they vote upon him and vote him in and make him a member?
turns.reading: These formulations originate in the examiner's one compound question.

turns.speaker: Hugh G. Bell
turns.reading: One tentative answer occurrence responds to the whole compound question. It is not three or four separate assents.

turns.speaker: Hugh G. Bell
turns.reading: Personal knowledge is not claimed. This does not mean NOT RECOGNIZED and does not erase the earlier reported-information state.

forward.carrier: 1902 consolidated Commission decision · Hugh claimant-specific section
forward.text: The later decision refers to Hugh's oral statement and testimony, characterizes what it attempted to show, and assesses what the testimony does not tend to establish. It does not quote the three recognition turns or preserve the examiner's council / vote / membership wording.
brakes: NEGATIVE SUFFICIENCY ASSESSMENT ≠ NEGATIVE HISTORICAL FACT.

machine_three.input: Hugh G. Bell's oral statement is the expressly selected input.
machine_three.characterization: The decision renders Hugh's attempted showing through birth, Mississippi residence, blood-fraction characterization, and reported information that his father was registered.
frame: whether his father was recognized by Choctaw tribal authorities in Mississippi as a member
whether his father or another alleged Choctaw ancestor complied or attempted to comply with Article Fourteen
machine_three.neighbor_brake: They are present in the evidence section. Their presence does not, by itself, make them prerequisites to this particular assessment.
machine_three.refusal_history: The decision's negative sufficiency assessment cannot be transformed into NOT RECOGNIZED, NOT REGISTERED, NOT CHOCTAW, NOT IDENTICAL, or CASE DENIED.
machine_three.refusal_case: This local assessment is not the complete case disposition. Follow the later decision acts separately.

joins.label: Robert ↔ Robert
joins.need: An independently earned identity bridge between the Public Lands occurrence and the MCR 879 family Robert.

joins.label: James ↔ James
joins.need: Evidence connecting the earlier James occurrence to the brother named in later family testimony.

joins.label: Levy ↔ Levi / Levy

bell_configuration.brake: The earlier manuscript independently contains the three Bell names. It does not state that they are related or identify them as the MCR 879 family.

states.state: reported / heard / told / saw a roll
states.text: Different witnesses carry different forms of knowledge. They are not one interchangeable proposition.

states.state: reported recognition + examiner-supplied wording + no personal knowledge
states.text: The recognition exchange preserves hearsay, supplied formulation, tentative response, and knowledge boundary.
The decision evaluates the testimonial reach and compares the family Robert with an older Article XIV Robert.
The Office states the administrative conclusion more explicitly as two Robert Bells.
The refusal is affirmed. This is administrative closure of the application, not a recovered answer to every historical question.
Witnesses repeatedly distinguish family memory from knowledge of Article XIV compliance or government land.
This record supplies the comparator the Commission tests against the family Robert.
The Commission rejects the proposed identity and treats the family showing as insufficient under the Article XIV frame it applies.
The later motion is denied pro forma as untimely; the Office says the record need not be transmitted to decide that motion.
